title: P0 Hosted API TTFB Slope Regression Investigation
content:
Summary:

On 2029-01-18 at ~02:12 UTC we observed a sustained, system-wide increase in time-to-first-byte (TTFB) for the Hosted API affecting both streaming and non-streaming requests. The degradation was classified P0 due to the breadth of traffic impacted and violation of the 99th percentile latency SLO for 18+ minutes. Approximate customer impact: 30% of requests had TTFB > 300ms (baseline ~50ms); a subset of streaming sessions experienced early fragment stalls. There were no large-scale 5xx spikes but elevated 502/504 rates to edge clients correlated with the same timeframe.

High-level impact:
- Elevated TTFB on edge-facing endpoints across regions (US-EAST and EU-WEST most affected)
- Streaming sessions: increased first-chunk latency and occasional fragment re-negotiation for ~12% of active sessions
- Sales/CS reported customer complaints for timeouts and slow chat load in affected windows

Detection and timeline (UTC):
- 02:11 — Synthetic probes (canary agents) start showing 2x baseline TTFB; SLO alert fires at 02:12
- 02:13 — Pager routed to SRE on-call; initial triage begins (edge → ingress → route selection)
- 02:15 — Observed rising leader-latency metrics on serving-runtime for prefix-hot keys; KV-cache hit ratio falling from 92% to 61%
- 02:18 — Routing fallback rate increases as edge tries alternative model variants. No immediate capacity saturation observed on GPU pools (utilization steady)
- 02:24 — Runbook step: scale ingress proxy instances and disable recent config-shared feature flag (kv-prefetch-optimizations-v2) as rollback candidate
- 02:29 — TTFB begins trending back toward baseline after flag rollback and eviction-window tuning; alerts resolved by 02:34

Root cause hypothesis (summary):
A recent control-plane rollout (config flip: kv-prefetch-optimizations-v2) introduced an aggressive KV prefetch and reduced per-prefix prefetch backoff. Under our typical traffic distribution this caused synchronized, high-volume KV cache prefetches for long-lived prefixes and hotspots. The resulting KV subsystem load increased lock contention and stretched request scheduling inside the serving runtime, increasing cold-key lookup latencies and producing higher TTFB. The prefetch behavior also amplified a small region-specific telemetry variance that led the edge to prematurely demultiplex streaming sessions more often, causing fragment re-assembly stalls.

Contributing factors and why mitigation was slow:
- Feature flag rollout was progressive but visibility into the per-prefix prefetch fanout metric was limited (metric introduced late in rollout)
- KV cache instrumentation captured hit ratio but not prefetch concurrency per-shard; this prevented quick root-cause attribution
- The adaptive batching/scheduling heuristic in the runtime prioritized tail-latency for token generation but did not account for transient KV RPC surge patterns, so scheduling latencies doubled under prefetch pressure
- Automated rollback thresholds were tuned for error-rate and CPU, not for KV RPC latencies or TTFB slope

Evidence gathered:
- Dashboards: prefix-hot metrics show sudden spike in prefetch RPCs peaking ~5x normal at 02:15 in us-east-1 and eu-west-1
- Traces: distributed traces show KV prefetch calls adding 120–300ms blocking time to request hot-paths; async token generation queues had elevated wait times
- Logs: control plane audit shows deployment of kv-prefetch-optimizations-v2 gated to 30% of instances at 01:50 with ramp to 60% at 02:05 (auto-ramp rule)
- Post-incident sampling: correlation between prefetch concurrency > 8 and requests with first-byte > 250ms is 0.82 Pearson

Immediate mitigations taken during incident:
- Rollback: Disabled kv-prefetch-optimizations-v2 gate at 02:24 (control-plane banner toggled off) — observable reduction in prefetch RPCs by 02:27
- Edge/ingress scaling: temporarily increased ingress proxy replicas in affected regions to reduce queueing for long TTFB requests (02:24–02:32)
- KV lease window softening: increased per-prefix backoff and reduced max prefetch concurrency in the runtime config to avoid thundering prefetch bursts (02:25)
- Short-term telemetry: enabled higher resolution sampling for KV RPC latency and per-shard prefetch counters for 2 hours post-incident (02:30)

Why rollback fixed it:
The rollout change directly changed client behavior towards the KV layer (more aggressive prefetch). Disabling the flag returned prefetch behavior to prior conservative defaults; with fewer concurrent prefetches the KV layer returned to stable lock contention levels and request scheduling normalized. Ingress scaling smoothed transient queuing while KV prefetch levels dropped.

Postmortem analysis and root cause (final):
Primary root cause: A control-plane gated feature (kv-prefetch-optimizations-v2) that altered prefetch concurrency/backoff was auto-ramped with insufficient per-prefix concurrency telemetry. The new prefetch profile causes synchronized, high-concurrency RPCs to KV shards which increased lock contention and request scheduling delays, manifesting as elevated TTFB.
Secondary factors: lack of automated SLO triggers based on TTFB slope or KV RPC latencies, and insufficient histogram-level visibility for per-prefix prefetch concurrency during rollouts.

Impact quantification:
- Duration: ~02:12 to ~02:34 window of visible customer impact; root-triggered prefetch RPCs peaked for ~9 minutes
- Requests affected: estimated 18–35% of active requests in impacted regions saw >2x TTFB; streaming sessions: ~12% experienced a first-chunk latency regression
- Customer-visible errors: 502/504 increased ~0.03% above baseline (helpful for support routing but not the main signal)

Longer-term action items (owners and ETA):
- Improve rollout telemetry: add per-prefix prefetch concurrency metric and histogram (Owner: Raj Patel, ETA: 2029-02-05)
- Update rollout gating: require kv-rpc-latency and TTFB slope SLO checks in the autopilot gate before auto-ramp beyond 30% (Owner: Sofia Martinez, ETA: 2029-02-01)
- Harden runtime scheduling: change adaptive scheduler to degrade prefetch priority when prefetch RPC concurrency exceeds threshold; add circuit-breaker for prefetch (Owner: Runtime team, listed as "runtime-scheduling" on the ticket, ETA: 2029-02-12)
- Runbook update: extend incident runbook with a section for 'prefetch storm' including quick flags to disable and safe temporary backoffs (Owner: Eng-SRE, Emma Chen, ETA: 2029-01-29)
- Automated SLO alerting: add TTFB-slope as a first-class signal with alert policy and paging thresholds (Owner: Observability team, Liam O'Connor, ETA: 2029-02-03)
- KB / Postmortem doc: publish final writeup in Confluence and notify CS for customer incident summaries (Owner: Emma Chen, ETA: 2029-01-25)

Draft runbook excerpt (prefetch storm mitigation) — for inclusion in Hosted API incident runbook:
1) If 99th TTFB > 2x baseline and KV prefetch RPCs/sec > 3x baseline for > 3 minutes:
   - Step A: Toggle control-plane flag "kv-prefetch-optimizations-v2" OFF for the affected fleet via rollout console (immediate)
   - Step B: Apply temporary per-prefix prefetch concurrency cap: prefetch_max_concurrency=4 (runtime config)
   - Step C: Scale ingress proxies by +25% if proxy-queue-depth > 50ms median
   - Step D: If streaming fragment stalls persist, temporarily increase streaming-session keepalive and enable fragment-reassembly-debug-sampling (to collect traces)
2) After toggles: monitor per-shard KV lock-wait histograms and TTFB 50/95/99 for 15 minutes before declaring mitigated

Followups and verification plan:
- Verify added telemetry in staging and a canary roll for the new per-prefix metric (observability sign-off)
- Re-run a simulated prefetch load test (kpreload-sim) against staging to validate circuit-breaker behavior
- Review rollout autogate thresholds: add TTFB-slope metric and require manual approval if prefetch concurrency is noisy across shards

Open questions (for longer-term discussion):
- Do we need to change data model for per-prefix metadata to allow more granular backoff tuning?
- Should prefetch be sharded with a randomized jitter to avoid synchronized bursts?
- What is an acceptable prefetch concurrency threshold across different instance classes and region topology?

Appendix (quick artifacts collected):
- Top traces: trace-20290118-02-15-001 (KV prefetch blocking path)
- Sampled logs: edge-ingress-us-east-02-15-sample.log (base64 chunked attachments in Confluence page)
- Dashboards: prefetch-rpc-by-prefix, ttfb-slope-by-region, kv-lock-wait-histogram

Notes to reviewers:
- This writeup focuses on the interplay between a behavior change (prefetch policy) and our runtime scheduling. The incident shows we have a blindspot in rollout telemetry for behaviors that produce high-concurrency workloads against shared state (KV). Please surface additional telemetry suggestions or alternative mitigations before merging to final postmortem in Confluence.

End of document.
